title: Add CLI version flag (--version, -v)
acceptance_criteria: Running the CLI with --version or -v anywhere in argv (standalone, or alongside/before a subcommand) prints 'fleet-e2e-toy v<version>' and exits 0, where <version> is read at runtime from package.json's version field (currently 1.0.0, so today's output is exactly 'fleet-e2e-toy v1.0.0') via require/import of package.json (resolveJsonModule already enabled in tsconfig) -- no second hardcoded copy of the version string anywhere in src/cli. Works without requiring a subcommand or hitting the network.

title: VERIFY: build + lint + full test suite
acceptance_criteria: npm run build (tsc), npm run lint, and npm test (jest, full suite including tests/cli/ integration tests) all pass cleanly with zero errors/warnings introduced by this sprint's CLI work. No console.log left in route handlers, no 'any' types introduced, CLI code follows repo conventions (res.status().json() pattern doesn't apply here since CLI has no server code, but error-wrapping/no-raw-stack-trace conventions from CLAUDE.md and requirements.md are upheld). This is the final checkpoint -- depends on every other task in this sprint.

title: CLI integration test suite
acceptance_criteria: A new tests/cli/ folder (per CLAUDE.md: all integration tests live in an integration-test folder, not scattered into unit test files) contains an integration suite that drives the built/compiled CLI as a subprocess against a live NoteAPI server on PORT 3001, matching this repo's npm run start:test convention (spawn the server, wait for GET /health per integ-test-playbook.md, run CLI subcommands via child_process against NOTEAPI_URL=http://localhost:3001, then tear the server down). Covers: each CRUD subcommand happy path, --version/-v, global and per-subcommand --help/-h, at least one blank/whitespace-arg rejection, at least one unknown-subcommand rejection, and at least one live API error (e.g. read of a nonexistent id) producing a clean non-zero exit with no raw JSON/stack trace on stderr. File(s) match jest's existing testMatch (**/*.test.ts) and roots (tests/) in jest.config.ts so 'npm test' picks them up automatically -- no jest.config changes needed. No unit-test-style CLI tests added outside tests/cli/.

title: CRUD subcommands: create, update, delete
acceptance_criteria: 'create --title <title> --content <content>' (both required, pre-network validated) issues POST /api/notes and prints the created note to stdout. 'update --id <id> [--title <title>] [--content <content>]' ('--id' required; title/content optional but at least one should be settable, pre-network validated) issues PUT /api/notes/:id and prints the updated note. 'delete --id <id>' ('--id' required, pre-network validated) issues DELETE /api/notes/:id and prints a confirmation to stdout. All three: on any API error (network failure, 4xx/5xx, including the {errors:[...]} validation-failure shape from POST/PUT) print a clear 'Error: ...' message to stderr via the shared error normalizer (never raw JSON, never a stack trace) and exit non-zero.

title: CRUD subcommands: list and read
acceptance_criteria: 'list [--tag <tag>] [--q <query>]' issues GET /api/notes with matching query params appended only when provided, and prints the returned notes to stdout in a readable form. 'read --id <id>' issues GET /api/notes/:id ('--id' required, validated pre-network via the shared validator) and prints the note to stdout. Both: on any API error (network failure, 4xx/5xx) print a clear 'Error: ...' message to stderr derived via the Task gh-toy-2fq.1 error normalizer (never a raw JSON error object or stack trace) and exit non-zero.

title: Shared input validation for required/blank CLI args
acceptance_criteria: A shared validation helper (in src/cli, alongside or reusing the skeleton from gh-toy-2fq.1 -- not duplicating src/utils/validation.ts which is server-side) rejects any required argument that is missing, empty, or whitespace-only BEFORE any network call is made, printing 'Error: ...' to stderr naming the offending flag and exiting non-zero. Missing required args (e.g. create without --title) are also rejected the same way pre-network. Applies uniformly so each CRUD subcommand task can call it for its required fields (read/update/delete: --id; create: --title/--content). No raw stack traces for any of these cases.

title: Help system (global + per-subcommand usage)
acceptance_criteria: Running the CLI with no args, or with --help/-h as the sole or leading arg, prints global usage (lists all subcommands: list, read, create, update, delete) to stdout and exits 0. Running '<cli> <subcommand> --help' or '<cli> <subcommand> -h' prints that subcommand's usage (its flags, which are required vs optional) and exits 0. Unknown subcommand name (not matching list/read/create/update/delete/--help/--version) prints a clear 'Error: unknown command ...' style message to stderr and exits non-zero -- never a raw stack trace. No network call made for any help path.

title: CLI entrypoint + HTTP client skeleton
acceptance_criteria: A src/cli/ entrypoint exists with an argv dispatch mechanism (subcommand name -> handler) and a shared HTTP helper module that issues requests to ${NOTEAPI_URL:-http://localhost:3000} using fetch/http, parses JSON responses, and normalizes API error bodies from BOTH shapes used by the server: {error: string} (404/generic 400) and {errors: [{field, message}, ...]} (POST/PUT validation failures) into a single clear message. No subcommands, help text, or --version need be wired yet, but the dispatch skeleton must have clear extension points for them. Unknown subcommand names produce a clear non-zero-exit error via this skeleton (no stack trace). package.json main/bin not required yet (separate task).

description: tests/integration/cli.integration.test.ts drives the exported dispatch() in-process against an ephemeral server, not the compiled dist/cli/index.js as a subprocess. This means the package.json bin wiring (gh-toy-2fq.2), main()'s process.exitCode assignment, and real stdio are untested. Add a smoke test that spawns the built binary against a live server and checks exit code + stdout.

title: CLI flag parser consumes next flag as a value
description: getFlag (src/cli/flags.ts) returns the next token unconditionally, so 'create --title --content foo' sets title="--content". Out of scope for gh-toy-2fq.5/.6 (flag parsing originates in .1/.4 and requirements.md does not specify this case), but worth tracking: guard against a value that is itself a known flag, or document the limitation.

title: Wire package.json bin entry for CLI
acceptance_criteria: package.json has a bin field (e.g. {"fleet-e2e-toy": "dist/cli/index.js"}) pointing at the compiled CLI entrypoint from Task gh-toy-2fq.1. tsc build (npm run build) produces that file. Running the built CLI directly (node dist/cli/index.js) or via the bin name after npm link/pack works without module-not-found errors. No changes to server bin/main.

title: Add config file support (~/.fleet-e2e-toy.yaml)
description: Allow users to persist default flag values in a YAML config file at ~/.fleet-e2e-toy.yaml so they don't have to repeat common flags on every run. Acceptance: reads config on startup, CLI flags override config, warns on unknown keys, documents supported keys in README.

title: Handle SIGINT gracefully (Ctrl-C)
description: The tool should catch SIGINT (Ctrl-C) and exit cleanly without a Python traceback or incomplete output. Acceptance: Ctrl-C prints 'Interrupted.' and exits with code 130, no stack trace shown, partial output files cleaned up.

title: Add JSON output mode via --json flag
description: Add a --json flag so all command output can be emitted as machine-readable JSON for scripting and CI pipelines. Acceptance: --json flag accepted on any subcommand, output is valid JSON, human-readable output is default, errors also JSON-formatted.
